scenes.tts: Myoglobin draws a hyperbola. Hemoglobin draws an S. Where does the S come from?
scenes.visual: Title fades. Myoglobin's hyperbola and hemoglobin's S on one axis. On screen: Where does the S come from?
scenes.narration: Myoglobin draws a hyperbola. Hemoglobin draws an S. Where does the S come from?

scenes.tts: Hemoglobin has four sites. And the whole molecule can take either of two overall shapes.
scenes.visual: A hemoglobin tetramer with four hemes; it splits into two silhouettes labelled T and R.
scenes.narration: Hemoglobin has four sites. And the whole molecule can take either of two overall shapes.

scenes.tts: T, for tense, is held by extra salt bridges between the subunits. Each heme in T holds oxygen weakly.
scenes.visual: T silhouette with salt bridges drawn as small links between subunits. Label: weak grip.
scenes.narration: T, for tense, is held by extra salt bridges between the subunits. Each heme in T holds oxygen weakly.

scenes.tts: R, for relaxed, has fewer of those bridges. Each heme in R holds oxygen tightly.
scenes.visual: R silhouette with fewer links. Label: tight grip.
scenes.narration: R, for relaxed, has fewer of those bridges. Each heme in R holds oxygen tightly.

scenes.tts: In one illustrative fit, a T site is half full only near one hundred ten torr. An R site is half full below one torr.
scenes.caption: In one illustrative fit, a T site is half full only near 110 torr. An R site is half full below 1 torr.
scenes.visual: Two faint hyperbolas: R rising almost at once (half full below 1 torr), T rising slowly far to the right (half full near 110 torr). Label: one illustrative fit.
scenes.narration: In one illustrative fit, a T site is half full only near 110 torr. An R site is half full below 1 torr.

scenes.tts: A molecule does not wait for oxygen to change shape. Even empty, it flickers between T and R.
scenes.visual: Empty molecules blinking between T and R outlines.
scenes.narration: A molecule does not wait for oxygen to change shape. Even empty, it flickers between T and R.

scenes.tts: But with no oxygen, T is far more stable. R molecules are almost absent.
scenes.visual: Population bar at zero oxygen: almost all orange T, a hairline of teal R.
scenes.narration: But with no oxygen, T is far more stable. R molecules are almost absent.

scenes.tts: So a sample is a mix. Its fullness is the average of each shape's fullness, weighted by how much of each is present.
scenes.visual: On screen: Y = f_R × Y_R + (1 − f_R) × Y_T. Each term highlighted as it is named.
scenes.narration: So a sample is a mix. Its fullness is the average of each shape's fullness, weighted by how much of each is present.

scenes.tts: At twenty torr, about a fifth of the molecules are R. Together the mix is about one-third full.
scenes.caption: At 20 torr, about a fifth of the molecules are R. Together the mix is about one-third full.
scenes.visual: Slider at 20 torr. Population bar: about 21% R. On screen: R site ≈ 98% full, T site ≈ 15% full, mix ≈ 33% full.
scenes.narration: At 20 torr, about a fifth of the molecules are R. Together the mix is about one-third full.

scenes.tts: At one hundred torr, nearly all the molecules are R. The mix is about ninety-eight percent full.
scenes.caption: At 100 torr, nearly all the molecules are R. The mix is about 98% full.
scenes.visual: Slider at 100 torr. Population bar: about 96% R. On screen: mix ≈ 98% full.
scenes.narration: At 100 torr, nearly all the molecules are R. The mix is about 98% full.

scenes.tts: Between those two points, about two-thirds is delivered. But notice what changed. The fraction of R climbed with oxygen.
scenes.visual: Delivered band between 98% and 33%: about two-thirds. The population bar's R share highlighted: about 0.2% at 5 torr, about 21% at 20, about 96% at 100.
scenes.narration: Between those two points, about two-thirds is delivered. But notice what changed. The fraction of R climbed with oxygen.

scenes.tts: Why? R holds oxygen far better than T. So each oxygen bound makes R a little more favorable.
scenes.visual: One T molecule and one R molecule each take an oxygen; the R one settles deeper into a stability well.
scenes.narration: Why? R holds oxygen far better than T. So each oxygen bound makes R a little more favorable.

scenes.tts: Oxygen is a reactant that only R uses well. Adding oxygen pulls the balance from T toward R.
scenes.visual: Equilibrium arrow T ⇌ R tipping right as O₂ is added.
scenes.narration: Oxygen is a reactant that only R uses well. Adding oxygen pulls the balance from T toward R.

scenes.tts: Follow one molecule as it fills. Each oxygen multiplies the odds of R by the same large factor.
scenes.visual: Odds table animating: 0 bound: T wins by millions to one; 1: tens of thousands; 2: a few hundred; 3: about even, R slightly ahead; 4: R wins by hundreds. Label: illustrative fit; the pattern is the point.
scenes.narration: Follow one molecule as it fills. Each oxygen multiplies the odds of R by the same large factor.

scenes.tts: That factor is how much more tightly R holds oxygen than T does.
scenes.visual: The two faint hyperbolas with the gap between their half-full points highlighted.
scenes.narration: That factor is how much more tightly R holds oxygen than T does.

scenes.tts: At low pressure, nearly everything is T. The curve follows T's weak curve and barely rises.
scenes.visual: The true curve drawn as the blend: at low pO₂ it hugs the faint T hyperbola.
scenes.narration: At low pressure, nearly everything is T. The curve follows T's weak curve and barely rises.

scenes.tts: Through the middle, each oxygen tips more molecules into R. Their empty sites fill easily. This is the steep part.
scenes.visual: Population bar sweeping from T to R as the curve climbs steeply between the two faint curves.
scenes.narration: Through the middle, each oxygen tips more molecules into R. Their empty sites fill easily. This is the steep part.

scenes.tts: At high pressure, nearly everything is R. The curve flattens onto R's curve near full.
scenes.visual: The true curve meets the faint R hyperbola near the top and flattens.
scenes.narration: At high pressure, nearly everything is R. The curve flattens onto R's curve near full.

scenes.tts: Predict. Suppose T and R held oxygen equally well. What shape would the curve have?
scenes.visual: The two faint hyperbolas slide together. Question on screen: same affinity, what shape?
scenes.narration: Predict. Suppose T and R held oxygen equally well. What shape would the curve have?

scenes.tts: A plain hyperbola. Oxygen would favor neither shape, so the mix would never shift.
scenes.visual: A single hyperbola. Population bar frozen. Label: equal affinities: Hill coefficient 1.
scenes.narration: A plain hyperbola. Oxygen would favor neither shape, so the mix would never shift.

scenes.tts: So cooperativity is oxygen shifting the mix toward the shape that binds oxygen best. The four sites share one shape, so a shift changes all four at once.
scenes.visual: The four sites drawn inside one outline that switches shape as a whole; the contacts between subunits glow as it switches.
scenes.narration: So cooperativity is oxygen shifting the mix toward the shape that binds oxygen best. The four sites share one shape, so a shift changes all four at once.

scenes.tts: The Hill coefficient scores how steep the S is at half full. Identical, independent sites score one. Hemoglobin scores about two point eight.
scenes.caption: The Hill coefficient scores how steep the S is at half full. Identical, independent sites score 1. Hemoglobin scores about 2.8.
scenes.visual: Steepness meter at the half-full point. Myoglobin: 1. Hemoglobin: about 2.8.
scenes.narration: The Hill coefficient scores how steep the S is at half full. Identical, independent sites score 1. Hemoglobin scores about 2.8.

scenes.tts: The score can be no larger than the number of sites. It measures steepness. It does not count anything.
scenes.visual: Meter with its maximum marked at 4 for four sites. Label: a score, not a count.
scenes.narration: The score can be no larger than the number of sites. It measures steepness. It does not count anything.

scenes.tts: Predict. A carrier as steep as hemoglobin, but with myoglobin's P fifty. How much would it deliver?
scenes.caption: Predict. A carrier as steep as hemoglobin, but with myoglobin's P50. How much would it deliver?
scenes.visual: A steep S drawn far to the left, near 2 torr. Lines at 100 and 20 torr. Question on screen: how much delivered?
scenes.narration: Predict. A carrier as steep as hemoglobin, but with myoglobin's P50. How much would it deliver?

scenes.tts: Almost none. Its steep part sits far below twenty torr, so it is still full in the muscle.
scenes.caption: Almost none. Its steep part sits far below 20 torr, so it is still full in the muscle.
scenes.visual: Both lines meet that curve at the top. Delivered band: almost none.
scenes.narration: Almost none. Its steep part sits far below 20 torr, so it is still full in the muscle.

scenes.tts: A hyperbola with hemoglobin's P fifty delivers only about a third. Hemoglobin needs both: an S, and an S in the right place.
scenes.caption: A hyperbola with hemoglobin's P50 delivers only about a third. Hemoglobin needs both: an S, and an S in the right place.
scenes.visual: Four-carrier table: myoglobin about 7%; hyperbola at P50 26 torr about 36%; steep curve at P50 2 torr almost none; hemoglobin about two-thirds.
scenes.narration: A hyperbola with hemoglobin's P50 delivers only about a third. Hemoglobin needs both: an S, and an S in the right place.

scenes.tts: The S comes from two shapes that differ in grip, and oxygen shifting the mix between them.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Two shapes that differ in grip, and oxygen shifting the mix, make the S.
scenes.narration: The S comes from two shapes that differ in grip, and oxygen shifting the mix between them.

scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Two shapes that differ in grip, and oxygen shifting the mix, make the S.
